summary: The change stops the analyzer from crashing on [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] types with duplicate or mixed keys: the contract diagnostics are reported and the offending member is skipped instead of throwing. All eight targeted analyzer tests pass. However, the field-handling guard is inverted (missing '!'), so int-keyed fields are silently dropped and duplicate int-keyed fields evade MsgPack005, and the full suite regresses with 14 newly failing generation tests. The change should not merge as-is.

requirement_verdicts.confidence_basis: The three F1 tests pass on head (missing key/MsgPack004, member type/MsgPack003, allow-private/MsgPack015), and the code reports these diagnostics for suppressed types before the suppress-source-generation early return, confirming no regression in contract-diagnostic reporting; they exercise non-crash paths, while the crash fix is evidenced under N1.

The SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnosticsAreNotReportedWhenSuppressed test passes on head expecting zero diagnostics, and the code suppresses AOT-only checks (line 989) and returns before the partial-class check (line 1383) for suppressed types.

The duplicate-int-key, duplicate-string-key, and mixed-key-kind tests for suppressed types pass on head with no analyzer crash, and the code now skips the offending member (continue) and guards the dictionary Adds, removing the crash paths; the separate field-omission defect (C1) is a silent omission, not a crash, and is reported separately.

findings.title: Int-keyed fields silently dropped; duplicate int-keyed fields not reported
findings.claim: In the field-handling branch, the guard is missing '!': line 1163 adds an int-keyed field only when its key is already present, but the first occurrence is never added (line 1163 is false), so ContainsKey never becomes true. As a result every int-keyed field is silently omitted from the serialization model and duplicate int-keyed fields never reach line 1154’s KeysMustBeUnique diagnostic (no MsgPack005, no crash, silent data omission). The equivalent property branch correctly uses 'if (!intMembers.ContainsKey(...))' at line 1023; the base code added unconditionally at line 1155, so head regresses field handling versus base as well.
findings.suggested_fix: Change line 1163 to 'if (!intMembers.ContainsKey(member.IntKey))' to match the property branch, so the first int-keyed field is registered and duplicates are reported once without crashing.

findings.title: Full test suite regresses: 14 generation tests newly fail on head
findings.claim: tests.full_suite reports 14 failed, 14 of which are “not failing on base” and 0 also failing on base. All are source-generator snapshot tests failing with “Expected source file list to match” and an unexpected extra generated file (MessagePack.GeneratedMessagePackResolver.g.cs). This violates REQ-2234-N2’s “no regressions in the existing test suite” clause; the root cause (why head changes generation output for previously passing types) is not established by the evidence given.
findings.suggested_fix: Investigate why head emits an extra/changed generated file for these types (test isolation, static resolver state, or a real generation-model change such as C1), restore baselines only after the cause is understood, and do not merge with existing-test regressions.
